html:
Mauretania was an ancient Berber kingdom in northwest Africa, covering northern Morocco and western Algeria, and later a pair of Roman provinces. Its people, the Mauri, gave Europe the word "Moors". It is shown here in 200 and 100 BCE.

Its kings traded with Carthage and lived beside the larger kingdom of Numidia to the east. King Bocchus I first backed his son-in-law Jugurtha against Rome, then handed him over to the Romans in 105 BCE, ending the Jugurthine War and gaining land as a reward.

Rome made Mauretania a client kingdom. In 25 BCE Augustus gave it to Juba II, a scholar king raised in Rome, who married Cleopatra Selene, daughter of Cleopatra and Mark Antony. They ruled from Caesarea, now Cherchell, and from Volubilis. Their son Ptolemy was killed by the emperor Caligula in 40 CE. After a revolt, Rome split the kingdom into two provinces, Tingitana and Caesariensis, in about 44 CE, becoming part of the Roman Empire.
